name: Fulafeallan

facts.text: Level 77, 30,000 health. Spawns four or five 'Part of Fulafeallan' when fought.
Ful 'foul' and feallan 'to fall'; the reading 'foul-falling' is to verify.

story: Fuladl's twin in the low passages, or its other half: the old keepers never decided. They called it Fulafeallan, the foul thing that falls, because it drops from the roof of the passage where the water seeps through. Like its kin it is only rot that learned to move, and like its kin it comes apart under a blade and keeps coming. The keepers' last records say they bricked up the wet passage and wrote its name over the bricks, so that no one would open it by mistake. The ogres cannot read. They opened it.
legend: Same as Fuladl: it splits when you cut it, so kill the pieces before they reach the casters. Look up before you walk under the wet stretch of roof, because that is where it waits. One raid, one rot at a time, never both.

lairEntry: Water drips from the roof. Not all of it is water.
atmosphere.realmFirstKill: Fulafeallan will drip no more in Krondon.

briefing: fulafeallan, same deal as fuladl. it splits, aoe the bits
aftermathWin: both rots done. krondon smells a bit better
aftermathLoss: the bits got us again. we never learn
rumour: [heard|someone said] fulafeallan drops off the ceiling in the wet tunnels
fuladl and fulafeallan. two rots, old names, same mess

loremasterTopic.text: The foul thing that falls, the keepers called it, for it drops from the wet roof of the low passages. It is kin to Fuladl and splits as Fuladl does.

chronicle.win: {realm}'s raid under {raidLeader} burned Fulafeallan out of Krondon's low passages in {minutes} minutes.
chronicle.loss: Fulafeallan fell on {realm}'s raid in the dark; {raidLeader} could not cut the pieces fast enough.
